title: Variables and basic types
summary: Names bind to objects; built-in scalar types include integers, floats, booleans, text and None.
syntax:
name = value
count: int = 0
ratio = 1.5
ready = True
missing = None
label = f"{name}: {count}"
rules: Assignment binds a name; it does not copy a mutable object.
Use == for value equality and is None for absence.
Type annotations do not enforce values at runtime.

references.title: Variables and basic types — official documentation

title: Lists, tuples, sets and dictionaries
summary: Choose an ordered mutable list, fixed tuple, unique set, or key/value dictionary.
rules: List indexing can raise IndexError; dictionary indexing can raise KeyError.
Dictionary keys and set members must be hashable.
Use .get for optional lookup; insertion order is preserved in dictionaries.

references.title: Lists, tuples, sets and dictionaries — official documentation

title: Indexing and slicing
summary: A slice selects a half-open range with an optional stride from a sequence.
syntax:
sequence[index]
sequence[start:stop]
sequence[start:stop:step]
sequence[::-1]
rules: The stop index is excluded; negative indices count from the end.
Slicing clips out-of-range bounds; single indexing raises IndexError.
List slices create a new list, not a view.

title: Comprehensions
summary: Comprehensions build lists, sets or dictionaries from an iterable with an optional filter.
rules: The expression precedes the for clause.
Use a generator expression for lazy consumption.
Prefer an ordinary loop when side effects or complex control flow obscure the task.

title: Branching and loops
summary: Indentation groups suites beneath conditional and loop headers.
rules: Use a colon and consistent indentation for suites.
range(stop) excludes stop.
break exits a loop; continue advances to its next iteration.

title: Functions and arguments
summary: Functions accept positional or named arguments and return values explicitly or None implicitly.
rules: Defaults are evaluated once; use None instead of a mutable list default.
/ makes preceding arguments positional-only; * makes following arguments keyword-only.
Use return to produce a result; annotations describe intended types.

title: Modules and packages
summary: Import modules or selected names; packages organize modules under qualified names.
syntax:
import package.module
import package.module as alias
from package.module import Name
from .sibling import helper
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
rules: Relative imports require a package context; run with python -m package.module.
Keep application startup under the __main__ guard.
Avoid import *; explicit names make dependencies visible.

title: Exceptions and error propagation
summary: Catch expected exception types, let unexpected failures propagate, and preserve causes when translating errors.
rules: Catch specific types rather than a bare except.
finally runs during normal return and exception propagation.
Use raise ... from ... to retain the original cause.

references.title: Exceptions and error propagation — official documentation

title: Classes and instance state
summary: Classes combine instance attributes and methods; __init__ initializes a new instance.
rules: self refers to the instance and is explicit in method definitions.
Mutable class attributes are shared; initialize per-instance collections in __init__.
Prefer composition when inheritance does not model a useful relationship.

references.title: Classes and instance state — official documentation

title: Dataclasses
summary: Dataclasses generate initialization and comparison methods from annotated fields.
rules: Use default_factory for mutable field defaults.
Frozen blocks assignment to fields; it does not deeply freeze their contents.
Dataclasses do not validate annotated values at runtime.

title: Generators and iteration
summary: A generator yields values on demand and resumes its suspended function on each iteration.
rules: A generator is consumed once; create another to repeat iteration.
yield suspends execution; return terminates the generator.
Use a context manager around resources consumed lazily.

title: Context managers and cleanup
summary: with scopes a resource lifetime; cleanup runs when the suite exits, including on exceptions.
rules: Use with for files and client objects supporting the protocol.
A contextmanager generator must yield exactly once.
Cleanup code should preserve unexpected errors rather than suppressing them accidentally.

references.title: Context managers and cleanup — official documentation

title: Type hints and narrowing
summary: Annotations describe contracts for tools; unions and protocols express optional values and behavior.
rules: Annotations are not runtime validation; use explicit checks or a validation library.
is not None narrows an optional value for static analyzers.
The type statement requires Python 3.12 or newer.

references.title: Type hints and narrowing — official documentation

title: Async tasks and cancellation
summary: Coroutines cooperate through await; tasks schedule coroutines on an event loop.
syntax:
async def operation():
    await other()
asyncio.run(operation())
task = asyncio.create_task(operation())
task.cancel()
try:
    await task
except asyncio.CancelledError:
    pass
rules: Use asyncio.run at a synchronous entry point, outside an already running event loop.
Cancellation is delivered at suspension points; await a cancelled task to finish cleanup.
Use finally or async with for cleanup; do not swallow CancelledError inside workers.

references.title: Async tasks and cancellation — official documentation

title: Paths and text files
summary: Path represents a filesystem path and offers explicit text/byte I/O and directory operations.
syntax:
path = Path("directory") / "file.txt"
text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
for entry in path.iterdir():
    ...
rules: Choose an explicit encoding for text.
I/O can raise OSError and decoding can raise UnicodeError; handle expected failures.
Convenience read/write methods close their files automatically.

references.title: Paths and text files — official documentation

title: Streaming file I/O
summary: open returns a file object; with closes it after sequential or buffered processing.
syntax:
with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
    for line in stream:
        consume(line)
with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
    stream.write(text)
rules: w truncates an existing file; use a to append.
Use binary mode for bytes and text mode for str.
Keep lazy iteration inside the with suite so the file remains open.

title: JSON serialization
summary: json converts supported Python values to JSON text and decodes text into Python values.
syntax:
text = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)
value = json.loads(text)
json.dump(value, stream)
value = json.load(stream)
rules: Decoding malformed text raises JSONDecodeError.
JSON objects have string keys; custom objects need an explicit conversion.
Decoding JSON alone does not validate an application schema.

title: CSV rows and columns
summary: CSV readers handle delimiters and quoting; DictReader maps header names to field strings.
syntax:
with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
    for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
        consume(row)
writer = csv.DictWriter(stream, fieldnames=columns)
writer.writeheader()
writer.writerow(record)
rules: Open CSV files with newline="" so the csv module handles newlines.
Fields are strings by default; convert and validate numeric values explicitly.
Catch csv.Error and conversion errors when processing untrusted rows.

references.title: CSV rows and columns — official documentation

title: Application logging
summary: Configure a handler once at application startup and obtain named loggers in modules.
syntax:
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
logger.info("processed %s rows", count)
logger.exception("operation failed")
rules: Libraries should obtain a logger rather than configure the application root logger.
Use formatting arguments so interpolation can be deferred.
exception includes traceback details and belongs inside an exception handler.

title: pytest fixtures
summary: Fixtures supply reusable setup by parameter name and can yield to guarantee teardown.
rules: pytest discovers test_ functions in test_ files.
Request fixtures by function argument; scope defaults to function.
Use tmp_path for isolated filesystem work; teardown follows yield. Requires pytest 8.4.2.

title: pytest parametrization
summary: parametrize runs one test for multiple named argument sets with separate failure reporting.
rules: The parameter names must match test arguments.
Use pytest.raises for expected exceptions.
Requires pytest 8.4.2; run through pytest rather than executing the module alone.

title: HTTPX clients and timeouts
summary: Reusable clients send requests with configurable timeouts and explicit status checking.
syntax:
try:
    with httpx.Client(timeout=httpx.Timeout(5.0)) as client:
        response = client.get(url, params={"page": 1})
        response.raise_for_status()
        payload = response.json()
except httpx.HTTPError as error:
    recover(error)
rules: A Timeout config controls connect/read/write/pool limits, not a total wall-clock deadline.
raise_for_status rejects error statuses; JSON decoding may fail separately.
Requires HTTPX 0.28.1; mock transports avoid external requests in the playground.

references.title: HTTPX clients and timeouts — official documentation

title: Async HTTPX and cancellation
summary: AsyncClient integrates HTTP requests with asyncio; cancellation propagates through awaited operations.
syntax:
async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0) as client:
    async with asyncio.timeout(10):
        response = await client.get(url)
        response.raise_for_status()
rules: Use async with to close client connections.
An asyncio timeout bounds the overall operation; HTTPX timeouts bound individual phases.
CancelledError should propagate through request workers. Requires HTTPX 0.28.1 and Python 3.13.

references.title: Async HTTPX and cancellation — official documentation

title: Pydantic validation
summary: Pydantic models validate external data and expose structured errors and serialization methods.
rules: Default validation may coerce compatible values; request strict validation when needed.
Use Field for constraints and inspect errors() for structured diagnostics.
Requires Pydantic 2.11.7; v1 APIs differ.

title: FastAPI JSON endpoints and request tests
summary: FastAPI routes combine typed request models with automatic JSON responses and request validation.
rules: Pydantic model arguments are validated request bodies; invalid input produces 422.
Use HTTPException for explicit HTTP failures and response_model for output contracts.
Requires FastAPI 0.116.1, Pydantic 2.11.7 and HTTPX 0.28.1 for TestClient; tests run in process.

references.title: FastAPI JSON endpoints and request tests — official documentation

title: Argument kinds and safe defaults
summary: Separate positional data from named options; allocate mutable defaults per call. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
def process(data, /, *, limit=10): ...
def collect(item, bucket=None): ...
process(*values, **options)
rules: Before / is positional-only; after * is keyword-only.
Defaults are evaluated once when the function is defined.
Duplicate/unknown keywords raise TypeError.

title: Identity, aliases and copying
summary: Assignment shares objects; shallow and deep copies have different nested ownership. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
alias = original
shallow = original.copy()
from copy import deepcopy
independent = deepcopy(original)
rules: is tests identity; == tests equality.
A shallow container copy retains nested references.
Deep copying is not a universal resource-cloning strategy.

title: Equality and truthiness
summary: Distinguish absent values from valid falsey values before applying defaults. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
if value is None: ...
if not sequence: ...
left == right
result = fallback if value is None else value
rules: Zero, empty containers and None are falsey.
or returns an operand; it can erase intentional zero or empty text.
bool is a subclass of int; strict domain checks may exclude it.

title: Structural match patterns
summary: Dispatch structured input using shape checks, bindings and guards. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
match payload:
    case {"kind": "add", "value": int(n)} if n > 0: ...
    case [first, *rest]: ...
    case _: ...
rules: Bare names capture rather than compare constants.
Mapping patterns allow extra keys; sequences exclude str/bytes.
Guards run after matching; int() also matches bool.

title: Decorators and wrapped functions
summary: A decorator replaces a callable, commonly with a wrapper enforcing a reusable policy. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
rules: Forward arguments and return values.
wraps preserves metadata and __wrapped__.
Apply wrappers deliberately; decorator order changes behavior.

title: Properties and validated attributes
summary: Expose computed values or enforce invariants when attributes change. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
rules: Use a separate backing attribute to avoid recursive setter calls.
A getter-only property rejects assignment.
Validate before updating to keep previous valid state.

title: Iterable and iterator protocols
summary: Iterables produce iterators; iterators yield values until StopIteration. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
iterator = iter(iterable)
value = next(iterator, default)
def __iter__(self): return self
def __next__(self): ...
rules: An iterator is consumed and normally not restartable.
Use a new iterator for each pass over a reusable iterable.
Raise StopIteration for exhaustion, not arbitrary input errors.

title: Generator send and cleanup
summary: Resume a suspended generator with a value, delegate iteration, and close owned resources explicitly. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
generator = producer()
next(generator)
result = generator.send(value)
generator.close()
yield from child
rules: Prime with next() or send(None) before sending a value.
close() injects GeneratorExit; release resources in finally.
A closed generator is exhausted; do not yield during GeneratorExit.

title: Text normalization and regular expressions
summary: Normalize text deliberately and use bounded regexes for known input formats. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
text.strip().casefold()
pattern = re.compile(r"...")
match = pattern.fullmatch(text)
pattern.sub(replacement, text)
rules: Raw strings reduce backslash escaping.
fullmatch validates the whole string; search finds a substring.
Regex is not a general parser; constrain hostile input and avoid pathological patterns.

title: Aware datetimes and time zones
summary: Represent instants with aware datetimes and convert explicitly between offsets. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
datetime.fromisoformat(text)
datetime.now(timezone.utc)
instant.astimezone(target_zone)
end - start
rules: Naive timestamps have no offset and cannot identify an instant alone.
Use zoneinfo for named DST zones; fixed offsets do not implement DST.
Subtract compatible aware values; validate input before conversion.

title: Decimal arithmetic and rounding
summary: Construct decimal quantities from text and select precision, rounding and validation deliberately. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
Decimal("1.25")
amount.quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
with localcontext() as context: ...
rules: Binary float inputs preserve their binary approximation.
Reject nonfinite values explicitly for money.
Context precision and traps affect operations; isolate local changes.

title: Counter, defaultdict and deque
summary: Count hashable values, group missing keys and manage bounded queues using specialized containers. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
from collections import Counter, defaultdict, deque
Counter(values).most_common(n)
groups = defaultdict(list)
queue = deque(maxlen=limit)
queue.popleft()
rules: Counter missing keys read as zero; arithmetic may discard nonpositive counts.
defaultdict factory runs on missing indexing, not get().
A bounded deque discards oldest entries; popping empty raises IndexError.

title: Lazy iterator workflows
summary: Compose lazy streams and group adjacent keys with explicit input ordering. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
chain.from_iterable(groups)
for key, values in groupby(sorted_rows, key=key_function): ...
pairwise(values)
rules: groupby groups consecutive keys, not all equal keys globally.
Group iterators share the underlying input; consume each promptly.
zip(strict=True) rejects unequal lengths instead of truncating.

title: Partial application and bounded caching
summary: Bind reusable options and cache pure computations with an explicit lifetime. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
configured = partial(function, option=value)
@lru_cache(maxsize=128)
def compute(key): ...
compute.cache_clear()
rules: partial still permits overriding bound keyword arguments.
Cache keys must be hashable; cached objects are shared.
Avoid caching I/O or mutable results without a clear invalidation policy.

title: Structured asyncio task groups
summary: Own related tasks in a group; await all children and handle grouped failures after sibling cleanup. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as group:
    task = group.create_task(operation())
result = task.result()
except* ValueError as failures: ...
rules: The first non-cancellation failure cancels siblings; exiting awaits cleanup.
Do not swallow CancelledError inside a child.
Event handshakes make ordering explicit without timing assertions.

title: Async deadlines and cancellation ownership
summary: Bound an owned operation with a deadline and distinguish deadline expiry from external cancellation. Supported baseline: Python 3.13.7.
syntax:
async with asyncio.timeout(seconds):
    await operation()
except TimeoutError: ...
task.cancel()
await task
rules: Catch TimeoutError outside the timeout context.
Timeouts request cooperative cancellation, not forceful thread termination.
Await tasks you cancel so their finally cleanup finishes.

title: NumPy construction and dtypes
summary: NumPy construction and dtypes. Python 3.13.7, NumPy 2.5.4 and pandas 3.0.6; see practical cards for complete executable tasks.
syntax:
import numpy as np
a = np.array(values, dtype=np.float64)
a.shape; a.ndim; a.dtype
np.zeros((rows, columns), dtype=np.int64)
rules: An ndarray has a fixed dtype and rectangular shape; explicit dtype conversion can reject text.
Integer arrays have bounded arithmetic; use an appropriate dtype and validate domain bounds.
A shape (0, n) preserves the column dimension despite having no rows.

title: NumPy indexing, views and copies
summary: NumPy indexing, views and copies. Python 3.13.7, NumPy 2.5.4 and pandas 3.0.6; see practical cards for complete executable tasks.
syntax:
view = array[start:stop]
isolated = array[start:stop].copy()
selected = array[[0, 2]]
np.shares_memory(array, view)
rules: Basic slicing normally shares the data buffer: assignment through a view can mutate the source.
Advanced integer/boolean indexing returns copies; copy() explicitly isolates a basic slice.
Bounds checking differs between slices and scalar/advanced indexing; an empty slice is valid.

title: NumPy broadcasting and shape contracts
summary: NumPy broadcasting and shape contracts. Python 3.13.7, NumPy 2.5.4 and pandas 3.0.6; see practical cards for complete executable tasks.
syntax:
scaled = matrix * factors
outer = left[:, np.newaxis] + right[None, :]
np.broadcast_shapes(matrix.shape, factors.shape)
rules: Align trailing axes: each pair must be equal or one; incompatible dimensions raise ValueError.
A (rows, columns) matrix times (columns,) scales columns; (rows, 1) scales rows.
Broadcasting may allocate a large result; these examples deliberately use tiny arrays and produce new buffers.

title: NumPy axis reductions
summary: NumPy axis reductions. Python 3.13.7, NumPy 2.5.4 and pandas 3.0.6; see practical cards for complete executable tasks.
syntax:
row_totals = matrix.sum(axis=1)
column_totals = matrix.sum(axis=0)
counts = np.isfinite(matrix).sum(axis=0)
np.divide(totals, counts, out=result, where=counts != 0)
rules: axis=0 collapses rows, axis=1 collapses columns; keepdims=True preserves a length-one axis.
An empty sum has identity zero; an empty mean needs an explicit policy.
Use a mask and explicit counts for missing observations; infinity is rejected in the mean task.

title: pandas typed CSV and missing values
summary: pandas typed CSV and missing values. Python 3.13.7, NumPy 2.5.4 and pandas 3.0.6; see practical cards for complete executable tasks.
syntax:
frame = pd.read_csv(path, dtype={"name": "string", "quantity": "Int64"})
missing = frame["quantity"].isna()
clean = frame["quantity"].fillna(0)
mask = (frame["quantity"] > 0).fillna(False)
rules: Nullable Int64/string dtypes preserve pd.NA; pd.NA cannot be converted to bool.
read_csv default NA tokens include empty fields; document the intended policy for text like NA.
Require expected columns and validate domain constraints after parsing; do not silently drop invalid rows.

title: pandas labels, positions and Copy-on-Write
summary: pandas labels, positions and Copy-on-Write. Python 3.13.7, NumPy 2.5.4 and pandas 3.0.6; see practical cards for complete executable tasks.
syntax:
frame.loc[label, column]
frame.iloc[row_position, column_position]
frame.loc[mask.fillna(False), "quantity"] = replacement
frame["score"] = scores  # aligns Series labels
rules: loc selects labels and includes slice endpoints; iloc selects positions with exclusive stop.
Boolean nullable masks treat NA as false; fillna(False) makes exclusion explicit.
pandas 3 uses Copy-on-Write: derived objects behave independently when mutated. Assign with one loc operation; chained assignment does not update the parent.
Series assignment aligns index labels, never positional order; validate coverage and unique labels first.

title: pandas grouping and aggregation
summary: pandas grouping and aggregation. Python 3.13.7, NumPy 2.5.4 and pandas 3.0.6; see practical cards for complete executable tasks.
syntax:
groups = frame.groupby("name", sort=True, dropna=False)
totals = groups["quantity"].sum(min_count=1)
summary = groups.agg(rows=("quantity", "size"), known=("quantity", "count"))
rules: dropna=False retains missing grouping keys; default dropna=True removes them.
sum(min_count=1) retains unknown for groups with no observed quantities; size counts rows and count skips missing values.
Sort explicitly for deterministic output; index labels determine transform alignment.

title: pandas validated joins and cardinality
summary: pandas validated joins and cardinality. Python 3.13.7, NumPy 2.5.4 and pandas 3.0.6; see practical cards for complete executable tasks.
syntax:
result = left.merge(right, on="key", how="left", validate="many_to_one", indicator=True)
result.sort_values("row_id", ignore_index=True)
rules: validate rejects unexpected duplicate keys before a many-to-many expansion; use one_to_one when both sides must be unique.
pandas matches null keys to null keys, unlike common SQL join semantics; these tasks reject missing keys.
Choose unmatched-row policy explicitly and sort by a stable unique business key, rather than relying on incidental merge order.
